Ideas — for architect review
R

What can move, and what it costs

This is an RC-frame house: the columns and beams carry everything, and every wall is non-loadbearing infill. That means walls can be added, removed, or moved between columns quite freely — with three rules that keep changes safe and cheap:

Interior partitions in 100 mm brick, not 200

decide now

Your solid clay brick at 200 mm weighs ≈ 4.4 kN per m² of wall — a single-wythe 100 mm partition (≈ 2.4 kN/m² plastered) halves the load on every slab and saves roughly half the bricks and mortar. Keep 200 mm only for the facades and for wet walls that carry pipework. Walls under 200 mm get hoop iron every alternate course — note 5 on your own drawings.

Heavy walls belong over beams

decide now

A wall standing on a beam line (the column grid) loads the structure the way it was designed. A wall standing mid-slab is a line load the slab may not have been designed for — any new 200 mm wall off the grid needs TIPSTEP's line-load check first. 100 mm partitions are generally fine anywhere, which is another reason to prefer them inside.

Stack the wet rooms

verify

Bathrooms and kitchens sitting above one another share one vertical pipe stack — cheaper, fewer slab penetrations, easier to fix leaks. Check with TIPSTEP that the first-floor baths sit over the ground-floor WC zone and the second-floor bath over the first-floor bath; small wall moves now can line them up before the plumbing is cast in.

Timing: brickwork is already rising on the ground floor. Ideas below are marked by urgency — anything tagged decide now only stays cheap while the relevant wall is not yet built.

G

Ground floor

Ventilate the garage — it sits under bedrooms

garagedecide now

Two cars inside the envelope need permanent through-ventilation: low vents near floor level and high vents near the slab on the external wall (louvred blocks with insect mesh work well in this brick). Without them, exhaust fumes and fuel smells migrate up into the house.

Solid, self-closing door between garage and foyer

garage → foyerdecide soon

The internal door from the garage side should be solid-core and self-closing — it is the fume and fire separation between cars and living space. A cheap hollow door here undoes the whole separation.

Give the WC real ventilation

foyer WCdecide now

The WC by the foyer is deep in the plan. If its wall doesn't reach the facade, it needs a vent duct to outside or a small extractor — a windowless, unvented WC in a solid-brick house stays damp and smells. If a facade window is possible, a high-level 400–600 mm louvre is the simplest fix.

Kitchen: window over the worktop + cross-vent to dining

kitchendecide soon

The kitchen sits in the corner with two external walls — use both: a window over the worktop for light and smoke, and keep a clear opening toward the dining windows so air crosses the space. If charcoal cooking is ever likely, add a permanent high vent too; it is much easier to build in now than to core-drill later.

Use the void for stack ventilation

living roomoptional

The living room has a double-height void above it. Put openable high-level windows at the top of the void (first-floor level): warm air rises and escapes there, pulling cooler air in through the ground-floor windows — free cooling in Kigali's climate, and it keeps the double-height space from becoming a heat trap.

Claim the under-stair space

internal stairoptional

The space under the 20-riser internal stair is a free store room (brooms, tools, water pump) — one 100 mm partition and a door. Cheap now, awkward to add later.

1

First floor

The shared bathroom needs air

bath between bedroomsdecide now

The bath serving bedrooms 1 and 2 is internal. Best: shift its layout so one wall touches the facade and take a high-level louvre window. If it can't reach the facade, plan a vertical vent duct or extractor now, while walls and slabs are still open — a wet room with no ventilation in solid brick will grow mould within a year.

Dressing room: borrowed light and a vent

master suitedecide soon

Closed cloth storage with no airflow gets musty. Give the dressing room a permanent vent above its door (the P.V. from your drawing notes) and, if the layout allows, a small high window or glazed strip borrowing light from the bathroom or bedroom side.

Balustrade the void properly

void edgedecide soon

The void over the living room needs a guard ≥ 1.0 m high with no climbable horizontal rails and gaps under 100 mm — think of visiting children. Decide now whether it's masonry (heavy — it stands on the slab edge beam, fine) or a steel/glass rail (lighter, more open).

Family room: keep both facades breathing

family roomoptional

It's the biggest room on the floor. Windows on its two external sides at opposite ends give real cross-ventilation; if furniture planning allows, keep the door zone toward the stair open (or use a wide opening instead of a standard door) so air moves through the whole floor.

Bedroom window rule of thumb

all bedroomsdecide soon

For each bedroom: glass area ≥ 1/10 of the floor area, openable area ≥ 1/20, plus the permanent vent above the window. Check bedroom 2 especially — mid-plan rooms tend to end up with one small window. Burglar bars + insect mesh on openable vents, as everywhere in Kigali.

2

Second floor

Treat it as a lockable independent unit

external stair landingdecide soon

This floor has its own living room and kitchen — a complete apartment served by the external stair. One lockable door at the stair landing turns it into rentable space or independent guest quarters without touching anything else. Decide before the landing walls are built.

Kitchen extract straight to outside

kitchen & diningdecide now

The unit's kitchen must vent directly through its external wall (window + permanent high vent, or a cowled duct). Never let it vent toward the terrace seating side — cooking smoke will own the terrace every evening.

The terrace is a roof — build it like one

terracedecide now

Falls of at least 1.5 % to rainwater outlets (two, so a blocked one doesn't flood), a proper waterproofing membrane turned up 150 mm at every wall, and a drip edge. This is the single most common leak source in Kigali houses — it's cheap in the screed stage and miserable to retrofit.

Terrace guard at 1.1 m, fixed into concrete

terrace edgedecide soon

This edge is two storeys up: guard height ≥ 1.1 m, and both the balustrade and the pergola posts anchor into a small RC upstand or the slab edge beam — never into brick alone. Brick holds no pull-out force; a leaned-on rail fixed to brick is how balcony accidents happen.

Shade the west glazing

living / terrace frontoptional

The big glass faces the afternoon sun. The pergola already helps; deepen it or add a slatted screen on the west edge and the living room stays usable at 4 pm without curtains drawn all day.

Water tank placement is a structural decision

roofdecide now

If a roof water tank is planned: 1 000 L is a 10 kN point load — it must sit directly over a column or on a beam, confirmed by TIPSTEP, never mid-slab. Decide the position now so the support can be cast with the roof, and so the plumbing stack lines up with the bathrooms below.

3

Penthouse — proposed studio apartment

Your idea: a third floor on the roof — one self-contained studio with a bedroom, sitting room, kitchen and toilet. It works, and it adds a second rentable unit — but only as lightweight construction, and only after a structural check. The house was designed as ground + 2 floors; the 200 × 200 columns are already working near their design load. Read the first card below before anything else.

Structural gate — this decides whether the penthouse happens. A brick-and-concrete third floor would roughly double what the columns and footings were asked to carry — not an option. A lightweight penthouse (steel or timber frame, sheet or board cladding, light insulated roof — no solid brick, no concrete roof slab) adds only ~15–20 % and is realistic. TIPSTEP must check the columns, the footings, and the +10.0 roof slab (designed as a roof, now becoming a floor) and sign the result before any material is ordered. Also: adding a storey means amending the construction permit — start that early.

Lightweight or nothing

whole penthousedecide now

Steel or timber stud frame, sheet/board cladding (fibre-cement, timber, or sandwich panel), light insulated roof. Walls + roof land around 0.8–1.2 kN/m² against ~6+ for brick and concrete — the difference between "checkable" and "impossible" for your 200 × 200 columns. The look can still be plastered-smooth to match the house.

Stack the wet core

toilet + kitchendecide now

Placing the penthouse toilet and kitchen on the west wall puts them directly over the second-floor bath and kitchen zone — one vertical stack serves four floors. Fix this position first; the rest of the layout can flex around it.

The stair continuation

west sidedecide soon

The external stair currently ends at the second floor. One more flight — steel, lightweight, landing clear of the studio door — completes independent access, which is what makes the penthouse a self-contained rental like the floor below it. Check headroom over the second-floor landing.

The roof slab becomes a floor

+10.0 slabdecide now

Roof slabs are designed for lighter live loads than floors. TIPSTEP must confirm the +10.0 slab for residential loading plus the frame walls — and the remaining terrace needs waterproofing, falls to two outlets, and a 1.1 m guard, exactly like the second-floor terrace rules.

Permit amendment

paperworkdecide soon

An added storey changes the approved drawings — Kicukiro district needs a permit amendment with the revised plans and the engineer's check. Cheap and routine if done before building; a fine and a stop-order if done after.

V

Windows & ventilation — the short rules

RuleNumberApplies to
Glass area≥ 1/10 of floor areaEvery habitable room
Openable area≥ 1/20 of floor areaEvery habitable room
Permanent vents (P.V.)above every door & windowWhole house — note 3 on your drawings
Cross-ventilationopenings on two sidesLiving, family room, kitchens, bedrooms where possible
Wet roomswindow, duct, or extractor — never sealedEvery WC, bath, kitchen
Garagelow + high permanent ventsGround floor garage (bedrooms above)
Securitymesh + bars on permanent openingsAll ground-floor and reachable vents

Kigali needs no heating and, with cross-ventilation and shading done right, no air conditioning. Every vent built into the brickwork now costs a few hundred francs; every one drilled in later costs a mason, a scaffold and a patch.

D

Elevations & section — for the window talk

Keep these two sheets at hand when discussing windows and vents with the architect — every opening idea above has to land on one of these facades, and the section shows the storey heights the vents and high windows work with.

Prepared 21 Aug 2026 from the TIPSTEP drawing set (Plan No. 8045) and site photographs. These are ideas to discuss with your architect and engineer — they are not instructions to build. Columns and beams are fixed; wall moves are free only where noted, and any new heavy wall off the beam grid needs the engineer's line-load check. Companion document: Parking Beam Jacket.
